threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'thank you' to the bus driver. In Dalston, that's a sign you’re not quite a local yet.
Heard a couple arguing about which way to get home, didn't realize they were on the wrong bus until the driver told them. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I found myself debating the best falafel spot while dodging a stray dog on the way to the bakery on Sonnenallee.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find an abandoned factory turned art space that hosts silent disco parties every Saturday. The vibe is unreal.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their disdain for the BART delays. A newbie just shrugs, but we’ve got stories of missed plans and frozen dinners.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus where a guy serenaded the whole ride with opera. Everyone groaned, then clapped when he hit a high note. Classic SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the plazas, but the real vibe is in the quiet streets where locals sip café amb llet in peace, away from the crowds.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones getting confused at the ‘tapa’ menu, asking if it’s all small dishes. The locals know better than to ask.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: Calling it the 'Tube' instead of the 'Underground' is a dead giveaway. Locals just call it the 'Overground' when it's not a hassle.
Caught the N68 home last night, and a group of teens turned an empty seat into a makeshift stage for an impromptu rap battle. Quite the show!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a group of kids playing football in the street while their parents gathered for a grill on the sidewalk. Classic Neukölln vibe.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg will you find a laundromat that doubles as a bar. You can sip a Berliner Pilsner while waiting for your laundry to spin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they don’t even flinch hearing the BART’s brakes screeching like a cat on a hot tin roof. It’s just background noise.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy juggling on the 19 bus today while a toddler giggled. That’s San Francisco – chaos and charm all in one ride.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just for tapas and bars, but it’s really the locals who cherish the hidden plaça where kids play and artists gather.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by their reluctance to squeeze onto the metro during rush hour, standing awkwardly by the doors instead.
